title: A mistaken eureka moment feels the same as a sound one

statements.text: A eureka moment about a mistaken idea should be able to bring happiness and conviction indistinguishable from one about a sound idea. The first feeling alone would not tell the two apart, and the attachment could outlast the moment by days or years.

prediction.resolution_criterion: A study of rare, emotionally intense insights, not task-based ones, finds that insights later judged mistaken came with happiness and conviction no different from those later judged sound, and that the attachment lasted beyond the moment.

sources.quote: Even when the idea is mistaken, such an experience should be capable of producing happiness and conviction indistinguishable from those accompanying a sound idea.
The initial feeling alone would not reliably distinguish the two, and the attachment could persist long after the moment itself.
